title: Port Forwarding to 127.0.0.1 on Windows Host not working
body:
### Issue Description

I updated from Podman to Podman 6.0.2 and since then port forwarding to the windows host does not work anymore. It still works using the IP of the podman machine. Also running a server inside the podman machine without containers works correctly.

Even a clean installation of Podman 6.0.2 did not solve the issue.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1.  Run `podman run --rm -p 8080:80 nginx`
2. Run `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 ` (should not work)
3. Run `Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 ` (should work)
4. Cancel execution
5. Run `podman machine ssh`
6. Run `python3 -m http.server 8080` inside podman machine (run directly without using containers)
7. Run `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 ` (should work)
8. Run `Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 ` (should work)

### Describe the results you received

Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 8080 does not work for containers, works without containers

Test-NetConnection <wslip> -Port 8080 works for both ways

### Describe the results you expected

I would expect podman containers to be reachable from Windows host network.

I just downgraded to Podman CLI v5.8.5 and it works fine.

We switched the port forwarding logic to better bind the ports in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/27311

The logic is actually required to properly work with ipv6 localhost connections and in general calling listen() on them was always wrong as we do not have actually logic to accept connections there which means the connections that ended up there (bypassing the firewall nat rules) would just hang.

So at least on the linux side I do not see us changing this by default. I guess we could consider adding an option to add the listen call back but I really like to avoid that if possible. A udp socket does not have listen() so how does the forwarding work there in WSL?

cc @l0rd @danishprakash

> A udp socket does not have listen() so how does the forwarding work there in WSL?

Doing a quick read of the WSL codebase I guess the answer is they do not support udp forwarding at all?
Same problem here - very annoying and blocks my work. So, I have to downgrade again...

As a workaround you can use podman machines IP address directly instead of 127.0.0.1.

You can get it with following command: `wsl hostname -I` (may return more than one IP when multiple wsl machines are running).

But yeah it is annoying to reconfigure everything. I think for most cases a downgrade is the best way.

You can run your machine rootless (which is the default when you use podman machine init from the cli, it is Podman Dekstop which defaults to creating rootful machines AFAIK). Unless you actually need a rootful machine (which is not needed in most cases) you can just run podman rootless which will bind+listen on ports like it always did because the port forwarded is in user space not via firewall rules.

Hi, i can confirm this regression in the following environment:

- **Windows:** 11, build `10.0.26200.8973`
- **WSL:** `2.7.11.0`
- **WSL kernel:** `6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- **Podman client:** `6.0.2`
- **Podman server:** `6.0.2`
- **Podman machine:** WSL-based, rootful
- **User mode networking:** enabled

Containers start successfully and their published ports are reachable from inside the Podman machine. Podman also reports the port mappings correctly. However, connections from Windows through `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` are refused.

The suggested alternatives, including using the Podman machine IP, switching to rootless or downgrading to Podman 5, are not suitable for our use case.

As a temporary workaround, we had to create detached Windows OpenSSH local-forwarding processes for all required TCP ports:

```text
Windows 127.0.0.1:<port>
    -> SSH
    -> Podman machine 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

This restores localhost access without changing container definitions, application configuration or existing data. The SSH tunnels must be recreated after restarting Windows or the Podman machine.

I can confirm this issue on Windows with Podman 6.0.2.

My environment:
- Windows 11
- WSL2 backend
- Podman Desktop with Podman 6.0.2
- Rootful machine
- UserModeNetworking=false

Symptoms are exactly the same as described in this issue:

- Container ports are published (e.g. -p 15672:15672)
- Services are reachable from the Windows host using the WSL IP address
- Services are NOT reachable through localhost / 127.0.0.1
- A regular process started directly inside WSL (for example `python3 -m http.server 8888`) is reachable through localhost

Additional troubleshooting performed:
- Recreated the Podman machine
- Removed and reinstalled Podman Desktop
- Removed the WSL distribution and recreated it
- Verified that WSL localhost forwarding is working
- Verified that container services are reachable through the WSL IP
- Tested both rootful and rootless modes (same result)

The definitive test was rolling back to the previous Podman Desktop release using Podman 5.x. After the rollback, localhost port forwarding immediately started working again without any other changes to Windows, WSL, or the containers.

This looks like a regression introduced in Podman 6.0.2 rather than a local configuration issue.

So assuming WSL will not fix the port detection on their end the only realistic option I see is add a new containers.conf option like `force_port_listen=true` and then in podman add a listen call when this option is set.
Then in podman-machine-os embed a containers.conf file which hard codes that option only for the WSL image.

Then it should work out of the box again for podman machine users on WSL.

Unless someone has a better idea how to fix this I guess I have to go for that even though I really do not like these special cases.

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/pull/295
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29451
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1065

should fix it when used together. Note this will need the new podman build with the option inside the image as well as the config file set there if anyone wants to test this.

I have tested #29451, and it fixes the problem.

But I have checked that configuring WSL to use [mirrored mode networking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking#mirrored-mode-networking) fixes the problem too. That requires manually editing the `~/.wslconfig` file, though.

[Using WSL mirrored-mode networking](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27643) is something @lstocchi wanted to use as an alternative implementation of the current user-mode networking support (which uses a sidecar WSL distribution), but we may want to have it as the default (when the version of WSL supports it).

you should not have to set this if you created a new machine with podman it should be set under /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d/999-podman-machine-wsl.conf

Also you have it listed under the `[containers]` section which is wrong, it is under `[engine]`.

once the container is running please run `ss -tulpn` in the wsl machine and share the output, and please copy paste terminal output. pictures are hard to read...

I think this is related to another thing I was talking about with @l0rd that wsl is unable to see dual stack ports, there is another config option that could help but it causes other problems when run rootless atm: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/pull/297/changes

The easiest workaround for that is passing an explicit bind ip for the port such as `-p 0.0.0.0:8080:80808`

The WSL Machine is not the problem, the container was always reachable there. The problem is the windows host binding, that the container is also reachable on windows. My understanding is that WSL's port forwarding daemon creates a host listener matching the socket family reported by the Linux kernel. 

When podman binds a port using a wildcard address 
(in the case above 
`tcp    LISTEN   0        0                       *:5433                 *:*`
) Linux defaults to IPv6 socket, so WSL creates a host listener matching it. 
(above 
`::1                                 5433      ::                                  0          Listen`
)

At this point if you run 
`Test-NetConnection ::1 -Port 5433` should succeed and  `Test-NetConnection 127.0.0.1 -Port 5433` should fail because nothing is listening on the IPv4 loopback interface on Windows.

To make 127.0.0.1 work as well, Podman needs to explicitly create an IPv4 socket when binding/listening on host ports (or explicitly bind IPv4 alongside IPv6) so that WSL creates the IPv4 127.0.0.1 listener as well on the Windows side.

because the kernel does not support ipv6 localhost dnat so yes `::1` is never expected to work when running podman as root.
That is the main reason why we need to NOT listen() on the sockets, so a connect to ::1 fails and the application falls back to ::1.

Because WSL does not know what non listing sockets are we need to work around by listen() again, that then means connecting to ::1 just hangs.


> Linux defaults to IPv6 socket, so WSL creates a host listener matching it.
> To make 127.0.0.1 work as well, Podman needs to explicitly create an IPv4 socket when binding/listening on host ports (or explicitly bind IPv4 alongside IPv6) so that WSL creates the IPv4 127.0.0.1 listener as well on the Windows side.

Well yes and no, it is WSL who has no idea that dual stack sockets are a thing. There is no reason an application has to bind `0.0.0.0` and `::` as two different socket, you can just bind `::` and by default that accepts both v4 and v6 addresses. There is an IPV6_V6ONLY only socket option one has to set to opt out of that even. so really it is WSL port detection that is broken https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/14154

In `ss` that means `*:$port` dual stack socket, `0.0.0.0:$port` ipv4 only, `[::]:$port` ipv4 only. We default to dual stack because well that is simply more efficient.
If you want split sockets that is what `default_host_ips = ["0.0.0.0", "::"]` is for and what I suggested we add to WSL as well, but well that need further bug fixes in rootlessport first.

And like I said the simple user work around to force ipv4 only is to pass something like `-p 0.0.0.0:8080:80808` to force a v4 bind only from podman with the listen fix that should be enough to have something working on podman 6.1. IF you do not need v6 at all just use `default_host_ips = ["0.0.0.0"]` as config option and then the rootlessport problem should not matter either
